question: How did Boston surgeons check that two brothers were truly identical before the first lasting kidney transplant, in 1954?
answer: Among other tests, by grafting a patch of skin from one brother onto the other. Skin from anyone else was rejected within weeks, so a graft that took meant neither immune system saw a stranger. Blood groups were matched and police compared fingerprints. Joseph Murray's patient, Richard Herrick, lived eight more years.
move: Check compatibility on something small before risking something vital.
reference: Merrill, Murray, Harrison & Guild, Successful homotransplantation of the human kidney between identical twins, Journal of the American Medical Association, 1956
